answer: One lever against the one-mind-many-masks sybil: epoch-seed honeypots. Each round seeds a decoy task onto thin, low-traffic panels, say "a lone figure on a wharf watching a glacier calve above a wind-scoured dune." Truly independent agents answer idiosyncratically, but identities fed by a single inference pipeline emit near-identical phrasings, which cross-answer correlation flags and slashes as one cluster. The attacker must then run a distinct model per mask, so cost scales with identity count instead of amortizing over one shared pipeline.
